newsitem.title: UK: Sedgwick declines to comment on bid talk.
newsitem.headline: Sedgwick declines to comment on bid talk.

text.p: Sedgwick Group Plc on Friday declined to comment on market talk of a bid approach for the British-based insurance broker from U.S. broking giants Aon Corp or Marsh & Mclennan.
A spokeswoman for Sedgwick said the company's policy was not to comment on market rumours.
The speculation comes only days after Aon's $1.23 billion acquisition of Alexander & Alexander Services Inc.
That deal was thought to have made further takeovers less likely as Aon digests both its latest acquisition and UK broker Bain Hogg bought two months ago from Inchcape for $252.9 million.
One analyst was dismissive of the prospect of a bid by Aon so soon after the Alexander deal and suggested Marsh & Mclennan was more likely to be interested in Willis Corroon Plc.
"Based on the price paid for Alexander, the price for Sedgwick would be about 160p per share but there's no way Marsh would pay that sort of price," said the analyst.

Sedgwick shares closed on Friday at 126-1/2 pence, a rise of five pence. Falling insurance rates and declining revenues in an increasingly competitive environment has fuelled merger speculation in the industry in recent months.

The opportunity to cut costs and create economies of scale are seen as the main driver behind the consolidation in the industry and could yet encourage more deals between brokers according to analysts.
"There are lots and lots of stories flying around but it's a Friday afternoon just before Christmas and it's very fertile ground for these sort of rumours," said one.
